title: BNK INFLAME Study - Secondary prevention of cardiovascular risk factors in cardiologists offices
summary:
Although numerous scientific studies have shown that the inflammatory marker hsCRP can play an important role in cardiovascular diseases, there has not yet been sufficient research into the actual significance of this value in the day-to-day practice of cardiology specialists in Germany.
In particular, it remains unclear:
How many patients have elevated hsCRP levels under normal clinical conditions.
Whether, and to what extent, elevated hsCRP levels influence the decisions of treating doctors.
This study aims to answer these open questions. To this end, data from day-to-day clinical practice will be collected and analysed. The aim is to examine whether the findings from scientific studies can be applied to everyday clinical practice and whether they are of benefit to the treatment of patients in that context.
conditions: nflammatory markers in patients with confirmed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease

interventions.name:
This prospective, multicentre, non-interventional study is being conducted in private cardiology practices. All examinations are carried out as part of routine check-ups without influencing patient selection, diagnostic investigations or therapeutic decisions (treatment, dosage, duration, etc.).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Signed informed consent form from the patient
Confirmed atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease: 
•    coronary heart disease and/or cerebrovascular occlusive disease (cAVK) and/or peripheral arterial occlusive disease (pAVK)
confirmed by:
-	Imaging (CT, carotid duplex ultrasound, MRA)
-    invasive diagnostics (coronary angiography, PCI)
Current hsCRP result available (< 3 months)
hsCRP measured outside the context of an acute illness
Exclusion criteria:
Existing pregnancy
Currently active cancer
Current acute infection
Immunomodulatory / immunosuppressive treatment (e.g. for COPD, rheumatic conditions, autoimmune diseases)
